# py-maidr

> py-maidr (PyPI package `maidr`) is a Python library that makes matplotlib, seaborn, Plotly, Bokeh, plotnine and Altair data visualizations accessible to blind and low-vision users through sonification, braille, text, and AI-powered conversational modalities. It is the Python binding of MAIDR (https://maidr.ai/), developed by the (x)Ability Design Lab at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; a sibling package exists for R (https://r.maidr.ai/).

maidr (pronounced "mader") patches matplotlib, seaborn and Plotly at import time, so users just `import maidr` and call `plt.show()` (or `maidr.show(plot)`) to get interactive HTML with keyboard-navigable sonification, braille, text, and AI chat; `maidr.save_html()` writes a standalone file. Its supported plot types are listed below, the stable ones first and then the experimental ones, each of which is marked [experimental] (see Plot Type Stability below). Works in Jupyter, Colab, VS Code, Streamlit, Shiny, Gradio, and Quarto.

**Stable**: bar, stacked bar, dodged bar, count, histogram, KDE, line, multi-line, step, pie, box, violin, heatmap, scatter, smooth/regression, candlestick, multi-layer, multi-panel, and facet plots.

**Experimental**: boxen [experimental], hexbin [experimental], contour [experimental], error bar [experimental], point [experimental], lollipop [experimental], area [experimental], stacked area [experimental], Gantt [experimental], word cloud [experimental], ROC curve [experimental]. These may change without a deprecation period; see [Plot Type Stability](https://py.maidr.ai/stability.html).

## Docs
- [Documentation Home](https://py.maidr.ai/): Installation, quick start, related projects and how to cite
- [Matplotlib/Seaborn Examples overview](https://py.maidr.ai/examples.html): Custom backend, keyboard shortcuts, links to every plot family
- [Bar Charts](https://py.maidr.ai/examples/bar.html): Bar, count, stacked and dodged bar charts
- [Pie Charts and Word Clouds [experimental]](https://py.maidr.ai/examples/pie-wordcloud.html)
- [Histograms and KDE Plots](https://py.maidr.ai/examples/histogram-kde.html)
- [Line and Step Plots](https://py.maidr.ai/examples/line-step.html)
- [Heatmaps, Hexbin [experimental] and Contour Plots [experimental]](https://py.maidr.ai/examples/heatmap-hexbin-contour.html)
- [Box, Boxen [experimental] and Violin Plots](https://py.maidr.ai/examples/box-boxen-violin.html)
- [Scatter and Regression Plots](https://py.maidr.ai/examples/scatter-regression.html)
- [Multi-Layer, Multi-Panel and Facet Plots](https://py.maidr.ai/examples/multi-layer-panel-facet.html)
- [Candlestick and Gantt Charts [experimental]](https://py.maidr.ai/examples/candlestick-gantt.html)
- [Shiny, Streamlit and Gradio Dashboards](https://py.maidr.ai/examples/dashboards.html)
- [Plotly Examples](https://py.maidr.ai/examples-plotly.html): Plotly-specific accessible plot examples
- [Bokeh Examples](https://py.maidr.ai/examples-bokeh.html): Bokeh accessible plot examples (Bokeh support is experimental)
- [plotnine Examples](https://py.maidr.ai/examples-plotnine.html): plotnine (ggplot2 grammar) accessible plot examples, passed as a `ggplot` to `maidr.show(p)` (plotnine support is experimental)
- [Excel Examples](https://py.maidr.ai/examples-excel.html): the charts of an Excel workbook (.xlsx), read without Excel by `maidr.read_excel_charts(path)` and passed to `maidr.show(chart)` (Excel support is experimental)
- [PowerPoint and Word Examples](https://py.maidr.ai/examples-office.html): the charts of a PowerPoint presentation (.pptx) or a Word document (.docx), read without PowerPoint, Word or Excel by `maidr.read_powerpoint_charts(path)` and `maidr.read_word_charts(path)` and passed to `maidr.show(chart)`; every chart type the Excel reader reads (PowerPoint and Word support is experimental)
- [TensorBoard Examples](https://py.maidr.ai/examples-tensorboard.html): the training curves, distributions, histograms, PR curves, hyperparameter sweeps, embeddings, profiles and Keras model graph of a TensorBoard log directory (Keras, TensorFlow, PyTorch), read without TensorFlow by `maidr.read_tensorboard_scalars(logdir)`, `maidr.read_tensorboard_distributions(logdir)` (as percentile bands [experimental]), `maidr.read_tensorboard_hparams(logdir)`, `maidr.read_tensorboard_projector(logdir)`, `maidr.read_tensorboard_pr_curves(logdir)` (as PR curves [experimental]), `maidr.read_tensorboard_profile(logdir)` (needs `xprof`) and `maidr.read_tensorboard_histograms(logdir)` (as ridgelines [experimental]), `maidr.read_tensorboard_graph(logdir)` (as a directed graph [experimental]) and passed to `maidr.show(chart)` and in a maidr tab of TensorBoard with `pip install maidr[tensorboard]` (TensorBoard support is experimental)
- [Keras Examples](https://py.maidr.ai/examples-keras.html): the training curves of a Keras model, drawn from what `model.fit` returns by `maidr.keras.plot_history(history)`, a classifier's confusion matrix by `maidr.keras.plot_confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred)`, a binary classifier's PR curve by `maidr.keras.plot_pr_curve(y_true, y_pred)` (as a PR curve [experimental]), the model's layers by `maidr.keras.plot_model(model)` (as a directed graph [experimental]), and `maidr.keras.MaidrCallback`, which keeps an accessible page up to date while the model trains (Keras support is experimental)
- [Weights & Biases Examples](https://py.maidr.ai/examples-wandb.html): the training curves of Weights & Biases runs, read from the runs' own `run-<id>.wandb` files without W&B or a network, or fetched from the W&B server, by `maidr.read_wandb_history(runs)` and passed to `maidr.show(chart)` (Weights & Biases support is experimental)
- [MLflow Examples](https://py.maidr.ai/examples-mlflow.html): the training curves of MLflow runs, read by `maidr.read_mlflow_metrics(runs)` from any tracking server, and an accessible chart stored in a run, where the MLflow UI shows it, by `maidr.log_mlflow_chart(chart, "charts/loss.html")` (MLflow support is experimental)
- [Altair Examples](https://py.maidr.ai/examples-altair.html): Altair (Vega-Lite) accessible chart examples
- [Plot Type Stability](https://py.maidr.ai/stability.html): Which plot types are stable and which are experimental
- [API Reference](https://py.maidr.ai/api/): show, render, save_html, stacked, close, set_backend, set_use_cdn, init_notebook, read_wandb_history, read_mlflow_metrics, log_mlflow_chart, Shiny, Streamlit and Gradio widgets

## Experimental plot families
These may change without a deprecation period; see [Plot Type Stability](https://py.maidr.ai/stability.html).

- [Area [experimental], Error Bar [experimental], Point [experimental] and Lollipop Plots [experimental]](https://py.maidr.ai/examples/area-errorbar-point-lollipop.html)
- [ROC Curves [experimental]](https://py.maidr.ai/examples/roc.html): scikit-learn `RocCurveDisplay`

## Optional
- [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/maidr/): Install with `pip install maidr`
- [GitHub](https://github.com/xability/py-maidr): Source code and issue tracker
- [MAIDR JavaScript core](https://maidr.ai/): The core library that powers py-maidr (npm package `maidr`)
- [maidr for R](https://r.maidr.ai/): The R package counterpart (CRAN package `maidr`)
